A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iterative story-visualization work, renamed from Story-Adapter to Story-Iter. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original story-visualization and subject-consistency experiments, component ablations, computational measurements, and human evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, variant evaluations, attention analyses, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The original initialization, GRCA, and linearly weighted external iteration remain substantively unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.4 adds an SDXL-LCM Fast variant using four diffusion steps and a ControlNet variant accepting pose maps. These introduce substantial extensions to inference and conditioning, beyond the method's renaming.

E1.justification: StorySalon, the twenty GPT-4o-generated 50/100-frame stories, and the 2,000 subject-consistency prompts are retained. V2 adds pose-conditioned visualization examples in Figure 9 and additional comic, film, and monochrome style scenarios in Appendix H.3, modestly broadening evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds IP-Adapter and IP-AdapterXL to the regular-length comparison. Table 2 adds FLUX.1.Kontext, Nano Banana, DALL·E 3, SEED-LLaMA, ConsiStory, and 1prompt1story to the long-story comparison. The original subject-consistent generation comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds four-step LCM evaluation, pose-conditioned testing, embedding Jensen-Shannon divergence tracking, and full-story time/memory comparisons. The original model's 50-step sampling, guidance 7.5, and ten iterations remain unchanged. Appendix C also changes the reported human-evaluation rubric from five criteria to four by dropping image quality; this does not establish that the study was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds attention maps and embedding-convergence analysis, four additional linear-weight ranges in Table 5, and sliding-window, random-reference, and mean-pooled aggregation ablations in Table 7. It also adds editing-model failure cases and a third-iteration result. The original GRCA-versus-CSA analysis is retained and expanded in Appendix A.5, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 Section 4.1 newly states that experiments use a fixed random seed by default, while Appendix H.3 mentions examples spanning different seeds. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the added disclosure does not demonstrate increased replication.

E6.justification: The proposed models' main benchmark scores are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive comparator, variant, efficiency, and ablation results. AR-LDM's StorySalon CLIP-T/aCCS/aFID changes from 0.237/0.683/40.25 to 0.239/0.684/42.55 in Table 1. Human image-quality scores are removed from v1 Table 5's counterpart, v2 Table 8, while the remaining ratings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same mathematical procedure. The explicit linear-weight formula restates the existing schedule, and Appendix B explains the previously used evaluation metrics. The new convergence discussion is empirical interpretation, without added formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free visualization up to 100 frames, improved consistency, and better interactions remain. V2 explicitly elevates the curated long-story benchmark to a main contribution and removes v1's abstract-level characterization of the framework as computationally efficient, qualifying efficiency elsewhere.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations involving embedding convergence, content-adaptive attention, and suppression of irrelevant references. It adds interpretations of editing-model failures and explicit diversity and runtime limitations. Appendix F changes v1's conclusion that ten iterations are optimal to suggesting fewer than ten suffice, and discusses adaptive stopping and weighting as future work.

D1.justification: V2 documents Grounding-DINO cropping and first-occurrence reference selection for the existing metrics, identifies NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware, and specifies StoryDiffusion's four reference frames. It updates code-access instructions to a repository and supplementary material. Most original hyperparameters and the pseudocode are retained, with their relocation alone constituting no reproducibility addition.

R1.justification: The broad diffusion-model survey is replaced by substantially expanded story-visualization positioning, including DreamStory, StoryGPT-V, MovieDreamer, and interactive-generation literature. Appendix E expands subject-consistency coverage, while the introduction and Appendix D develop distinctions from IP-Adapter and reference-image editing models. These exceed citation or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and substantial introduction and method prose, consistently distinguishes external iterations from diffusion steps, and adds an explicit contribution list. Related work is reorganized, pseudocode and implementation details move to the appendix, and dedicated variants, reproducibility, limitations, and disclosure sections reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds attention, convergence, pose-control, metric-extraction, and editing-failure displays, and replaces the main long-story comparison with a different illustrated comparison. The original combined ablation table is split and extended, while the human-evaluation table loses its image-quality column. Numerous retained figures and tables are also relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for GRCA through controlled aggregation and weighting ablations and comparisons with relevant additional methods. Full-story timing and Fast-variant results expose the practical speed-quality tradeoff missing from v1's per-image efficiency analysis, while metric documentation improves transparency. These gains outweigh the removal of human image-quality ratings and unclear per-image versus per-story FLOP accounting in Table 6, although those issues limit the revision's quality.
